title: From Raw Data to Real Business Impact: Mastering Power BI and Microsoft Fabric with Thummalacherla Krishnakanth
description:
Power BI projects often struggle not because of the visuals but because of weak data quality, modeling and performance foundations. In this interview, Fabric Super User and Senior Power BI Developer Thummalacherla Krishnakanth shares practical guidance for beginners and BI developers on star schemas, Power Query versus DAX, optimization, Microsoft Fabric and staying relevant in the AI era.
In this episode
00:00 – Welcome and guest introduction02:06 – From electrical engineering to data04:36 – Power BI in the age of AI and versus Excel10:30 – Common Power BI mistakes: data quality and modeling16:53 – Star versus snowflake schema, Power Query versus DAX24:42 – Performance, governance and Microsoft Fabric31:25 – AI in BI, enterprise projects and stakeholders47:05 – Certifications, community and rapid-fire round
Key takeaways
Many Power BI problems start before the visuals: check data quality and data types in Power Query or at the source, and model clean relationships from dimension to fact tables.A star schema with fewer, denormalized dimension tables connected directly to fact tables is the recommended default over a snowflake schema for performance.AI can help analyze and explore data, but strong fundamentals, certifications such as PL-300 via Microsoft Learn and close stakeholder contact remain what keeps data professionals relevant.
Worth quoting
“So in the means we will be having a less number of dimension tables getting directly connected to the fact tables so I would suggest to go with the star schema as a best practice.” – Thummalacherla Krishnakanth (19:24)
